finding: The new reuse rule fires when plan/DECISIONS.md holds any entry 'for that decision', not only an entry recording this same change. A fix that changes a frozen SDD decision an earlier slice already superseded in another direction then reuses the old entry and writes no entry for the new change. Example: D-3 changed SDD section 8 row X to return 404; this fix, a two-way door, changes the same row to return 410; step 7 finds D-3 'for that decision', reuses it, and the 410 change reaches neither the ledger nor the end-of-run audit.

The case the reuse targets is narrower: fixed key f073 names the entry fix Phase 1 step 2 recorded for this same fork.
fix: Narrow the condition: 'when plan/DECISIONS.md already holds an entry that records this same change (the caller recorded it before the procedure ran), reuse it instead of writing a new entry; a different change to that decision gets a new entry.'

finding: Possible misclassified result: the new restart-failure exit returns `blocked` in every step, including a restart on the fixed tree in step 4's restored run or step 5. When the fix itself stops the app from starting (for example, it adds a dependency the unit tier never wires), the procedure reports `blocked`, which tells the caller the procedure could not go on and the failure stays unfixed, instead of `fail`, which tells it the fix did not hold. The fix's edits stay in the tree either way.
why: skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:230-231 "`fail` | a check other than an adversary reproduction stays red after the fix (step 5) | The fix did not hold"; "`blocked` | the procedure cannot go on ... | The failure stays unfixed". A restart that succeeded on the reverted tree and fails on the fixed tree is evidence against the fix, not an environment blocker.
fix: Split the exit: a restart that fails on a tree without the step 3 fix → restore the fix, then `blocked`; a restart that fails on a tree with the fix → `fail`, naming the restart and its output.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/IN-PLACE-FIX.md:43-47 "A check that runs against the running instance runs, in any step, only after the caller's restart command has restarted that instance on the current working tree. A live check with no instance or no restart command handed over, or whose restart fails → restore the step 3 fix when a step reverted it, then return `blocked`, naming the check and any restart output."; :116-118 "Watch each test this step adds fail with the step 3 fix reverted, then pass with it restored; the record holds both runs. A live-tier test follows 'Live tiers' (quoted with double quotes in the file) for each of the two runs."
